title: U.S. House · California's 5th District
area: Covers part of the Sierra Nevada, including areas around Amador County, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Tom McClintock (R) placed first with 61.3% (129,653 votes) and Michael Masuda (D) placed second with 24.3% (51,418 votes) out of 211,542 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: Tom McClintock
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with a majority of votes cast
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2023, prior district); Chair, Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement

priorities.text: Fiscal reform, having proposed changes to curb unauthorized appropriations, control mandatory spending, balance the budget and protect the nation's credit.
priorities.quote: has proposed major fiscal reforms to curb unauthorized appropriations, control mandatory spending, balance the budget and protect the nation's credit

priorities.text: Immigration enforcement, chairing the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and authoring legislation to expand deportation grounds for criminal gang members.
Reducing regulatory barriers to housing construction, attributing high housing costs in part to construction mandates, permit limits and land-use restrictions.

positions.summary: Opposed H.R. 8, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act, in a House floor speech, describing it as a web of laws aimed at law-abiding gun owners.
positions.quote: HR 8 is brought to us by the same organizations and politicians who have made no secret of their intention ultimately to strip law-abiding citizens of their right to defend themselves.

positions.summary: Authored the Deport Alien Gang Members Act, which creates grounds of inadmissibility and deportability for aliens who are members of criminal gangs and bars them from asylum and other immigration relief.
positions.quote: The legislation creates clear grounds of inadmissibility and deportability for aliens who are members of criminal gangs or who have promoted, aided, conspired with, or participated in gang activities.

positions.summary: His campaign website calls for complete repeal of the Affordable Care Act, to be followed by tax advantages for individuals, Health Savings Accounts and other changes.
positions.quote: There is no substitute for its complete repeal.

record.text: Chairs the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources' Federal Lands and Water, Wildlife and Fisheries subcommittees, and on the House Committee on the Budget, for the 2025-2026 session.

Authored the Deport Alien Gang Members Act (H.R. 175), which passed the House Judiciary Committee in June 2026 and establishes grounds of inadmissibility and deportability for members of criminal gangs.

candidates.name: Michael Masuda
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Engineer; former U.S. Department of State Foreign Affairs Officer

priorities.text: Describes himself as an engineer rather than a politician, focused on effective solutions for the diverse valley, foothill, mountain, and desert communities of the district.
priorities.quote: I am an engineer, not a politician. I am focused on addressing our shared challenges and building a future for everyone to prosper.

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of living by targeting housing, healthcare and energy costs.
priorities.quote: Target major cost drivers: housing, healthcare, and energy

priorities.text: Wildfire prevention, including forest management and fuels reduction.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says he opposes unpredictable tariffs that raise costs and hurt farmers.
positions.quote: Oppose unpredictable tariffs that raise costs and hurt farmers

statements.quote: If we’re serious about affordability, we have to build more housing, make it less expensive to build, and make sure families can actually afford to stay in the communities they call home.
statements.context: On his campaign issues page, Housing section

statements.quote: My approach is simple: secure the border, enforce the law, and fix the system so it is orderly, timely, and works for our economy.
statements.context: On his campaign issues page, Immigration section

statements.quote: Protect Medicare and Medi-Cal Reduce barriers to obtaining and keeping coverage
statements.context: On his campaign issues page, Healthcare section

researchNotes: Tom McClintock has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his official House website's per-topic issue pages mainly aggregate vote notes, speeches and press releases rather than standalone position statements, so documented positions here are drawn from that vote-note and speech content. Masuda has not held prior public office. Biography gaps: McClintock's official biography gives no birth, education or pre-legislature career details (those come from Ballotpedia and Wikipedia); Masuda's campaign website was not loaded, so his biography rests on his Ballotpedia survey.
